# Explanatory note: restricted authority

This note explains how to complete a restricted power of attorney. It is guidance only and does not itself appoint anyone. The specimen form deliberately contains no names, contact details or personal identifiers. A completed instrument must be prepared separately and checked before it is signed.

1. Describe the permitted transaction precisely. A general reference to administrative assistance may be insufficient where the intended act involves collecting property, inspecting records or signing a receipt.
2. State the expiry mechanism. A fixed date, completion of the transaction or written revocation may be appropriate. Avoid suggesting that an unsigned draft already grants authority.
3. Distinguish reimbursement of reasonable expenses from permission to enter a new contract. A spending limit of GBP 250 is an illustration and should be replaced only after instructions are confirmed.
4. Explain whether delegation is permitted. Silence on that point should not be treated as an unrestricted right to appoint a substitute.

The terms Principal and Attorney describe capacities in the specimen. The word Witness describes the signing function.

Section 4.2, article 17 and schedule 1 are cross-references in this note. The proposed signing date of 18 December 2026 is an example of an ordinary execution date. Leave every personal-details field blank when circulating this explanatory copy.
